messages:
maya: Heads-up — prepublish CI for the sample-app just failed during the publish step, looks like a regen diff is blocking npm publish for the v1.4.0 cut. Logs below.

ci-bot: CI: workflow/sample-app-release #482 failed — regendiff check failed (see https://ci.redwood/482).

maya: regendiff summary pasted from CI:
```
Regendiff: typegen/definitions.ts
- interface User { id: string; name?: string }
+ interface User { name?: string; id: string }

Reason: nondeterministic property ordering from codegen->typegen.
Changelog check: changelog.md unchanged. Release stamp aborted.
```

thomas: ugh — ordering-only diffs again. Is this the openapi->codegen sorting flake we saw last quarter?

alex: probably similar cause. The codegen output isn't stable across runs when optional props are emitted in different positions. That triggers typegen to reorder, which our regendiff flags as a change.

maya: npm publish error from the job:
```
> npm publish --access public
ERR_PUBLISH_BLOCKED: release-stamp found regen diff in workspace/sample-app — aborting publish
```

sara: I'll take this — reproducing locally now. Quick idea: can we run `yarn typegen --stable-order` before committing? If not, we should normalize generated files as part of the regenscript.

thomas: two quick mitigation options:
1) revert the last generated commit that bumped types and republish (fast but clobbers any legit changes).
2) add a post-regen normalizer that sorts object keys and optional props consistently, and pin the typegen/codegen version in the sample-app workspace so CI runs the same binary.

alex: I think option 2 is better long-term. Also: we should avoid forcing a semver change for pure ordering-only diffs — maybe the release-stamp should detect "nondeterministic ordering" diffs and treat them as no-op for version bump. But that has risk.

maya: The blocking step is `scripts/ensure-clean-publish.sh` which currently treats any regendiff as a blocker. We could special-case diffs that match a regex of only ordering changes, but I'd prefer preventing the diffs in the first place.

sara: repro steps: cloned repo, ran `yarn install`, then `yarn workspace sample-app regen` -> got same diff. Local run: `git status` shows modified `packages/sample-app/src/types/generated.ts` only reordering props. I added a tiny script that runs `prettier --sort-keys` (not a real command but shows intent) and the diff goes away. Pushing branch now — `fix/sampleapp-regendiff`.

ci-bot: Started: CI run for branch fix/sampleapp-regendiff (#483).

maya: Thanks @sara. Can you also include a short note in the PR describing why this is nondeterministic and link to the codegen issue? We need an audit trail for the release team.

sara: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sample-app/pull/483 — includes normalization script and pins `@redwood/codegen` to 3.2.1 in the workspace package.json. Also added a regen smoke test to CI that runs twice in a row to catch nondet runs.

thomas: taking a look now. Left a small nit about the script path. If CI passes I'll merge.

alex: long-term action item: add a stable-key ordering pass in the typegen pipeline so generated TS doesn't change position across runs. Also add a changelog rule: if only whitespace/order diffs detected, don't auto-bump minor/major for generated-only changes. We'll sync on the RFC.

maya: Agreed. For the immediate release, prioritize getting this PR merged so the publish can proceed. cc @release-team.

thomas: Reviewed and approved, merging once green. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: CI finished: all checks passed for PR #483.

thomas: Merged and triggered release pipeline. Publish step retried, should be unblocked now.

maya: Confirmed — publish completed, v1.4.0 is out. Thanks everyone.

alex: follow-up: filing a small RFC to add deterministic ordering to typegen and a changelog policy for generator-only reorders.

sara: filing RFC now.

maya: Closing the loop — great job.
